nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets. If $L$ is a regular language over $\Gamma$, then its alphabet preimage $\{w \in \Sigma^* \mid f^*(w) \in L\}$ is regular, where $f^*(w)$ is the word obtained by applying $f$ to each letter of $w$.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under alphabet preimages

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets, $f^* \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ the monoid morphism that applies $f$ to each letter of a word, and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. Then the alphabet preimage of $L$ under $f$ equals the inverse image $(f^*)^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid f^*(w) \in L\}$ of $L$ under $f^*$.
nodes.title: Alphabet preimages are inverse images under word morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets, $L$ a language over $\Gamma$ with syntactic monoid $M(L)$, and $\varphi \colon \Sigma^* \to M(L)$ the alphabet preimage morphism, which sends a word $w$ to the class in $M(L)$ of the word $f^*(w)$ obtained by applying $f$ to each letter of $w$. If two words $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ satisfy $\varphi(x) = \varphi(y)$, then $x$ and $y$ are syntactically congruent…
nodes.title: The alphabet preimage morphism refines the preimage's syntactic congruence

The alphabet preimage morphism of $f$ and $L$ is the monoid morphism from the free monoid $\Sigma^*$ to the syntactic monoid of $L$ that sends a word $w$ to the syntactic class of $f^*(w)$, the word obtained by applying $f$ to each letter of $w$. It is the composite of the letterwise map $f^* \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$…

nodes.title: Division map for the syntactic monoid of an alphabet preimage

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. The alphabet preimage of $L$ under $f$ is the language over $\Sigma$ consisting of the words $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ such that $f(a_1) f(a_2) \cdots f(a_n) \in L$.
nodes.title: Alphabet preimage

nodes.summary: Let $e \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a bijection between alphabets and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. The syntactic monoid of the alphabet preimage $\{w \in \Sigma^* \mid e^*(w) \in L\}$, where $e^*(w)$ is the word obtained by applying $e$ to each letter of $w$, is finite if and only if the syntactic monoid of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the syntactic monoid is invariant under renaming letters

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then the syntactic monoid of the alphabet preimage $\{w \in \Sigma^* \mid f^*(w) \in L\}$ is finite, where $f^*(w)$ is the word obtained by applying $f$ to each letter of $w$.
nodes.title: Alphabet preimages preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then the syntactic monoid of the inverse image $h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Inverse images under word morphisms preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $e \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a bijection between alphabets and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. The alphabet preimage $\{w \in \Sigma^* \mid e^*(w) \in L\}$, where $e^*(w)$ is the word obtained by applying $e$ to each letter of $w$, is regular if and only if $L$ is regular.
nodes.title: Renaming letters by a bijection preserves and reflects regularity

nodes.title: The alphabet preimage morphism recognizes the alphabet preimage

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \Sigma \to \Gamma$ be a map between alphabets, $L$ a language over $\Gamma$, and $K$ the alphabet preimage $\{w \in \Sigma^* \mid f^*(w) \in L\}$, where $f^*(w)$ is the word obtained by applying $f$ to each letter of $w$. If $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are words such that $f^*(x)$ and $f^*(y)$ are syntactically equivalent for $L$, then $x$ and $y$ are syntactically equivalent for $K$.
nodes.title: Syntactic equivalence pulls back along an alphabet map

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids, $L$ a language over $\Gamma$, and $K = h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$ its inverse image. If $x, y \in \Sigma^*$ are words such that $h(x)$ and $h(y)$ are syntactically equivalent for $L$, then $x$ and $y$ are syntactically equivalent for $K$.
nodes.title: Syntactic equivalence pulls back along a word morphism

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids. For every word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n \in \Sigma^*$ (including the empty word, $n = 0$), we have $h(a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n) = h(a_1) h(a_2) \cdots h(a_n)$, the concatenation of the images of its letters.
nodes.title: Word morphisms act letter by letter

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids. If $L$ is a regular language over $\Gamma$, then its inverse image $h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under inverse word morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. The inverse image $h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$ consists exactly of the words $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n \in \Sigma^*$ such that the concatenation $h(a_1) h(a_2) \cdots h(a_n)$ of the images of their letters lies in $L$.
nodes.title: Letterwise description of the inverse image under a word morphism

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. Write $[u]_L$ for the class of a word $u$ in the syntactic monoid $M(L)$ of $L$, $K$ for the inverse image $h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$, and $\varphi \colon \Sigma^* \to M(L)$ for the recognizing morphism $w \mapsto [h(w)]_L$. This is the monoid morphism from the submonoid…
nodes.title: Division map for the syntactic monoid of an inverse image

nodes.summary: Let $\Sigma$ and $\Gamma$ be alphabets, $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ a monoid morphism between their free monoids of words, and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$. The inverse image of $L$ under $h$ is the language $h^{-1}(L) = \{w \in \Sigma^* \mid h(w) \in L\}$ over $\Sigma$.
nodes.title: Inverse image under a word morphism

nodes.summary: Let $h \colon \Sigma^* \to \Gamma^*$ be a monoid morphism between free monoids and $L$ a language over $\Gamma$ with syntactic monoid $M(L)$. The recognizing morphism of $h$ and $L$ is the monoid morphism $\Sigma^* \to M(L)$ that sends a word $w$ to the syntactic class $[h(w)]_L$ of $h(w)$; it is the composite of $h$ with the syntactic morphism of $L$.
